I’m not going to spread myself too thin this year. I only have 9.5 mu and three people in the house, and at my age I can still work the land, but I don’t want to gamble on too much high-labor crop area. Cotton is still my backbone because I know it well and it fits our land. Cauliflower gives earlier cash, so I’ll keep a small piece for that, but not too much because it needs more watching for water, worms, and disease. Stevia can make money if the buyer is steady, so I’ll plant some, but I won’t give it the biggest area because the market is not as solid as cotton. Since I have well irrigation, I’m not as scared of a dry spell, but pumping costs money, so I’ll water at the important stages, not carelessly. For fertilizer, I usually follow what worked in past years and what people around me are doing. I don’t chase the highest yield, I chase a stable harvest and money left in hand.

For cotton, I’ll keep the largest area, use a familiar hybrid seed, put most fertilizer as base with one or two topdressings, and irrigate a couple of times if rain is short. For cauliflower, I’ll use purchased seedlings on a smaller plot because it brings quicker income, but I’ll control spending and not overdo fertilizer. For stevia, I’ll keep a moderate area, manage weeds carefully, and use enough fertilizer to keep leaves growing, because that crop is for leaf yield, not just surviving. I’m balancing cash, labor, and risk this year. If I put too much money into inputs, then I feel tight later; if I cut too much, the field shows it. So I’ll stay close to my usual practice, with only small adjustments.
